verification_report.summary: The proof is correct, with the smooth/reduced conclusions conditional exactly as stated on the canonical-collar bridge and the nonreduced addendum conditional on the rigid zero-atom lemma and reduced classification. The canonical-collar prefix legally localizes ordinary CLD forms and cutoffs through analytic moment blocks, constructs exact primitive virtual-annular rays with finite branch separation, and proves the global-in-U exact collar preimage identity. The rigid zero-atom argument, Euclidean edge-flux calculation, residual-divisor comparison, and normalization/conductor analysis then give the smooth and reduced current classifications and the stated continuous-psh Bedford--Taylor independence. For the new nonreduced addendum, reduction leaves analytic points, tropical moments, ordinary/G-form calculus, compact-test topologies, positive-current Borel products, currents, and psh sheaves unchanged. Integration instead records the generic cycle multiplicities, yielding delta_X=sum_i m_i delta_i while the reduction has all coefficients one. Transferring the reduced classification gives every positive closed current as a unique locally finite nonnegative sum of the component currents. Finally, either the multiplicity-weighted or unweighted curvature equality forces each component signed curvature measure to be supported on the locally finite rigid conductor preimage; the zero-atom lemma kills those measures, proving the exact curvature equivalence and the continuous-pair Bedford--Taylor conclusion. All cited CLD, Ducros, Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff, and Tate statements match the definitions and hypotheses used.
